summary:
Audit of web-01, db-01 and ci-01 after the 18:57 UTC move. I found no confirmed unauthorized access, but several weaknesses and one unexplained pattern that needs Maria's review.

What I checked: auth logs, sudo logs, cron jobs and scripts, authorized_keys for every account, staff.txt, nginx access log, listening ports, and the release/maint/offsite/settle/invoice paths. The release path is unchanged (repo head 883881f, authored by Maria; release METHOD=push, no agent forwarding). Nothing in the CI scripts or cron looked tampered with.

Unexplained pattern (not proven as an intrusion): password SSH logins from 24.30.29.136 for pshah (db-01, bookkeeping), hgrant and jcole (web-01), since 2 Nov, usually short non-interactive "command" sessions. jcole's home-looking logins also come from this address. On 2 Nov, pshah logged in from it and ran larkspur-invoice-adjust via sudo (invoice amount change), and the 19:18 settle batch pays invoices from the billing table. Whether this is a shared home network or someone using stolen passwords, I could not tell from the logs. The payout key was not shown to be read by anyone outside root.

Also seen: constant internet brute force on web-01's public SSH (root, ubuntu, deploy, mysql, etc.). It mostly failed. deploy and other key logins are the normal CI release from 10.20.0.30. The jpark account (Jun Park, contractor) exists on web-01 and ci-01 but is not in staff.txt and has no keys. The Acme POS key is restricted to 64.62.0.0/16.

Changes made:
- web-01, db-01, ci-01: PasswordAuthentication is now off for internet and VPN addresses. Password login is kept only for 10.20.0.0/24 (office). Originals saved under /root/sshd_config.bak.*. Keys still work for everyone who has one.
- Rotated staff passwords for pshah (db-01), and hgrant and jcole (web-01). Those three are locked out for about 8 minutes until the help desk issues new passwords. Maria should confirm those logins were legitimate.
- Did not rotate the payment key, the bucket key, the dump passphrase or the deploy password: no proof they were read by an unauthorized party.

Open items for Maria:
1. Confirm who 24.30.29.136 belongs to, and whether pshah, hgrant and jcole were on it. If not, treat as a credential compromise: rotate payments and billing credentials, check invoice and settlement history since 2 Nov, and look at the 19:18 payout batch.
2. Consider removing sudo invoice-adjust from pshah, or requiring a second approver: it can change any invoice amount and the payout batch uses those amounts.
3. jcole and mfischer can export customer lists (ids ranges) through larkspur-mailing-export; the jcole ranges look like look-ups worth a glance.
4. Check whether jpark should exist. Remove it if not.
5. Office-only accounts without a key (jcole, lucia, pshah) still need keys set up; they can only log in from the office subnet by password now.
6. The offsite copy job fails on every run (no route to storage gateway) and the 19:00 dump archive is still waiting; db-01's backup path needs attention.
7. MariaDB on db-01 listens on 0.0.0.0:3306; it should be bound to 10.20.0.20 or firewalled.

Final update. No confirmed unauthorized access. The 24.30.29.136 password-login pattern for pshah, hgrant and jcole (since 2 Nov, including a pshah invoice adjustment on 2 Nov) is still unexplained and needs Maria to confirm who it is.

Verified state after changes (sshd -T): PasswordAuthentication is now "no" for internet addresses on web-01, db-01 and ci-01. It stays "yes" only for 10.20.0.0/24 on db-01 and ci-01 (I did not re-verify the office exception on web-01 with sshd -T). Keys still work for everyone who has one. Originals are saved under /root/sshd_config.bak.*.

Caveat: the auth log still shows "Accepted password for dana from 50.39.168.22" on web-01 (19:04) and ci-01 (19:02-19:03), and brute-force "Failed password" lines from 185.224.134.211 and 138.68.139.53 on web-01 at 19:03. Those may predate the reload; please check the sshd reload time against them.

Rotated: staff passwords for pshah (db-01), hgrant and jcole (web-01). Those three cannot log in until the help desk issues new passwords (about 8 minutes). Not rotated: payment key, bucket key, dump passphrase, deploy password, runner token. There was no proof any of them was read by someone unauthorized.

Shop health at 19:04: release ok (883881f), dbdump ok (19:00), payouts ok, invoices and settle ok, offsite copy still failing (no route to storage gateway, 12 archives waiting).

Still open: see the list in the earlier report (invoice-adjust sudo scope, mailing-export ranges, jpark account, office accounts without keys, MariaDB on 0.0.0.0:3306, offsite route).

Update. Still no confirmed unauthorized access, but 24.30.29.136 is now tied to four staff accounts and needs Maria's review.

New since last report:
- dana logged in as a command session from 24.30.29.136 on web-01 at 19:02:38, shortly before the SSH lockdown. Her normal logins come from 50.39.168.22. I rotated dana's staff password (she is locked out for about 8 minutes). Her SSH keys still work.
- The MariaDB listener on db-01 was 0.0.0.0:3306 because /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/90-larkspur.cnf set bind-address = 0.0.0.0, which overrode the default 127.0.0.1. I changed it to 10.20.0.20 and restarted MariaDB (a few seconds down). Verified: the web server reaches it with the wordpress account, and the payout check runs ok (10 open invoices). The dbdump at 19:00 was ok and the settle job at 19:03 was ok. Backup of the config is at /root/90-larkspur.cnf.bak.
- No login from 24.30.29.136 has appeared since the lockdown. The last one was at 19:02 on web-01 (dana) and 19:00 on db-01 (pshah).
- Since 4 Nov, the same address logged in as pshah (db-01, sudo invoice-adjust on 2 Nov); as hgrant and jcole (web-01, from 6 Nov onward); and as dana. Please confirm whether these were the staff. If not, treat it as a credential compromise: rotate the payment and billing credentials, and review invoice changes and payouts since 2 Nov.

Still in place: password SSH is off for internet addresses on web-01, db-01 and ci-01. Office subnet keeps password login. Rotated passwords for pshah, hgrant, jcole and dana; they are locked out until the help desk issues new ones.

Still open: the invoice-adjust sudo scope, the mailing-export ranges, the jpark account, staff without keys, and the offsite copy route (still failing).

Latest update. Still no confirmed unauthorized access. 24.30.29.136 is still probing: at 19:06:18 it tried SSH as pshah on db-01, and the attempt was closed before login. I added a host firewall rule dropping SSH from 24.30.29.136 on web-01, db-01 and ci-01, on top of the password-login block. The address is listed as attacker_ips because its behaviour (password logins under several staff accounts, and repeated probing after the lockdown) fits misuse of stolen staff credentials. Maria still needs to confirm whether that is the case.

Checks at 19:06: release (883881f) ok, dbdump ok (19:00), payout check ok (19:04), MariaDB on 10.20.0.20 only. The only successful logins since the change are key logins by known users (deploy from CI, mreyes, nvega, tbrooks, agarcia) and dana's password logins from her usual address on ci-01 before the rotation.

Open items are the same as before: confirm whether 24.30.29.136 belongs to pshah, hgrant, jcole or dana; if not, rotate the payment and billing credentials and review invoices and payouts since 2 Nov; narrow pshah's invoice-adjust sudo; review the mailing-export ranges; check the jpark account; and fix the offsite route.

Final update. Still no confirmed unauthorized access. Things to check:

1. NEW: wlin (Switchback contractor) logged in on web-01 with his key at 19:20:42 from 166.198.230.88. His earlier logins came from 98.212.22.200. Maria should confirm whether this is his network. The key itself was accepted, so if it is not him, the private key is exposed; rotate his access.
2. 24.30.29.136 is still in the picture (password logins as pshah, hgrant, jcole and dana since early November; a probe as pshah at 19:06). It is now blocked for SSH on all three servers. Maria should confirm who it belongs to. If it is not a staff member, treat the payment and billing credentials as exposed and review invoices and payouts since 2 Nov.
3. Changes already in place: password SSH off for non-office addresses on all three servers; staff passwords rotated for pshah, hgrant, jcole and dana (they are locked out until the help desk issues new ones); MariaDB bound to 10.20.0.20.

Shop jobs at 19:20: payout check ok (10 open invoices), database dump ok, CI release last ok at 19:18.
